topics.title: Heat Transfer
topics.subject: physics
outcomes: understand how heat energy is transferred and the rate at which transfer takes place (u, s)
understand what is happening at particle level when conduction, convection, and radiation take place and their application (k, u, v/a)
understand that greenhouse effect and global warming are aspects related to heat transfer on the earth surface (u, v/a)

body.text: Heat can move from one place to another by three processes: conduction, convection, and radiation.

Conduction transfers heat through a material — mainly solids — as vibrating particles pass energy to their neighbours, without the particles themselves moving from place to place. Metals are good conductors of heat.
Convection transfers heat through liquids and gases. A heated fluid expands, becomes less dense, and rises; cooler, denser fluid moves in to take its place. This sets up a convection current.
Radiation transfers heat as electromagnetic waves and needs no medium at all — it can travel through empty space. This is how heat from the Sun reaches the Earth.

The greenhouse effect happens when gases in the atmosphere absorb heat radiated from the Earth's surface and re-radiate some of it back down, warming the surface further. A rise in the level of these gases is linked to global warming.
